# package server

```go
import "github.com/otfabric/go-iec104/server"
```

Package server implements the controlled station (outstation, slave) of IEC 60870-5-104.

A [Server](#type-server) accepts connections and runs the protocol machine of each one in a [Session](#type-session). ASDUs received in control direction are passed to a [Handler](#type-handler); [Mux](#type-mux) routes them by type identification and rejects what the application does not serve, as the standard requires.

	mux := server.NewMux()
	mux.HandleFunc(asdu.C_IC_NA_1, func(s *server.Session, req *asdu.ASDU) {
		_ = s.Confirm(req)
		_ = s.Send(s.Context(), asdu.New(asdu.CauseInterrogatedStation, req.CommonAddr,
			asdu.MeasuredFloat{IOA: 4001, Value: 49.98}))
		_ = s.Terminate(req)
	})
	srv, err := server.New(mux, server.WithCommonAddrs(1))
	if err != nil { ... }
	log.Fatal(srv.ListenAndServe(":2404"))

A [FileServer](#type-fileserver) registered for FileTypes serves files to controlling stations.

Events are queued with [Server.Enqueue](#func-server-enqueue): each redundancy group delivers them in order to its one started connection and keeps them until the controlling station has acknowledged them. [Session.Send](#func-session-send) and [Server.Broadcast](#func-server-broadcast) send immediately and buffer nothing. All methods are safe for concurrent use.

### type File

```go
type File struct {
	Sections [][]byte
}
```

File is the content of a file a station offers, in sections. The controlling station calls the sections one after the other and acknowledges each.

#### func NewFile

```go
func NewFile(data []byte, sectionSize int) File
```

NewFile splits data into sections of sectionSize octets; the last one holds what remains. A sectionSize of 0 or less makes one section. Empty data makes a file without sections. The sections share the memory of data.


Len returns the length of the file in octets.

### type FileServer

```go
type FileServer struct {
	// Sink, when not nil, takes the files controlling stations send. Without
	// it a file ready is refused. Set it before the server starts.
	Sink FileSink

	// Directory, when not nil, answers a call of the directory (F_SC_NA_1
	// with cause "request") with the entries it returns, sent as F_DR_TA_1.
	// ioa is the address the call names, 0 for the default directory. The
	// last entry is marked as such for the caller. Returning no entries, or
	// leaving Directory nil, refuses the call. Set it before the server
	// starts.
	Directory func(s *Session, ca asdu.CommonAddr, ioa asdu.IOA) []asdu.FileDirectoryEntry

	// OnDone, when not nil, is called when a transfer ends: with nil once
	// the controlling station acknowledged the file, with
	// [ErrFileNotAcknowledged] or the error that stopped it otherwise. It
	// is not called for a transfer that ends because its session did. Set
	// it before the server starts.
	OnDone func(s *Session, ca asdu.CommonAddr, ioa asdu.IOA, name uint16, err error)

}
```

FileServer is a [Handler](#type-handler) for the file transfer services of IEC 60870-5-101, 7.4.11: it serves files to controlling stations (monitor direction), takes files from them (control direction, with [FileServer.Sink](#func-fileserver-sink)) and answers calls of the directory (with [FileServer.Directory](#func-fileserver-directory)).

A controlling station fetches a file like this:

	select file      F_SC_NA_1 (SCQ 1)  ->  F_FR_NA_1  file ready
	request file     F_SC_NA_1 (SCQ 2)  ->  F_SR_NA_1  section ready
	request section  F_SC_NA_1 (SCQ 6)  ->  F_SG_NA_1  segments, then
	                                        F_LS_NA_1  last segment
	ack section      F_AF_NA_1 (AFQ 3)  ->  F_SR_NA_1  next section, or
	                                        F_LS_NA_1  last section
	ack file         F_AF_NA_1 (AFQ 1)

and delivers one like this, the station doing the calling:

	file ready       F_FR_NA_1          ->  F_SC_NA_1 (SCQ 2)  call file
	section ready    F_SR_NA_1          ->  F_SC_NA_1 (SCQ 6)  call section
	segments         F_SG_NA_1, then
	last segment     F_LS_NA_1 (LSQ 3)  ->  F_AF_NA_1 (AFQ 3)  ack section
	last section     F_LS_NA_1 (LSQ 1)  ->  F_AF_NA_1 (AFQ 1)  ack file

A file the [FileSource](#type-filesource) does not have, or the [FileSink](#type-filesink) does not accept, is refused by mirroring the request with cause "unknown information object address". A length or checksum that does not match what arrived is acknowledged negatively. A session transfers any number of files at once, one per address and direction; starting an address again starts over. Transfers end with their session.

Register it for FileTypes:

	mux.Handle(server.NewFileServer(source), server.FileTypes...)

Deletion is not served: such a call is answered negatively.

### type Handler

```go
type Handler interface {
	HandleASDU(s *Session, a *asdu.ASDU)
}
```

Handler processes the ASDUs a controlling station sends.

HandleASDU is called from a single goroutine per session, in the order the ASDUs arrived; different sessions are served concurrently. It may call any Session or Server method. While it runs, later ASDUs of the same session wait, so long-running work belongs in its own goroutine.

A handler that panics has its session closed; the server keeps running.


HandlerFunc adapts a function to a [Handler](#type-handler).


HandleASDU calls f.

### type Mux

```go
type Mux struct {
	// contains filtered or unexported fields
}
```

Mux is a [Handler](#type-handler) that routes ASDUs by type identification and answers what the application does not serve the way the standard prescribes:

  - a type without a registered handler is mirrored with cause "unknown type identification"
  - a cause of transmission that is not valid for the type in control direction is mirrored with cause "unknown cause of transmission"

Handlers therefore only see requests they are expected to act on. A handler that does not know the addressed object answers with [Session.Reject](#func-session-reject) and [asdu.CauseUnknownIOA](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/otfabric/go-iec104/asdu#CauseUnknownIOA).

The zero Mux is ready to use and is safe for concurrent use.

#### func WithASDUParams

```go
func WithASDUParams(p asdu.Params) Option
```

WithASDUParams overrides the ASDU layout. IEC 60870-5-104 fixes it to [asdu.IEC104](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/otfabric/go-iec104/asdu#IEC104), so this is only needed for non-conformant peers or to set the time zone of time tags with [asdu.Params.In](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/otfabric/go-iec104/asdu#Params.In).

#### func WithAccept

```go
func WithAccept(f func(remote net.Addr) bool) Option
```

WithAccept installs a filter for incoming connections, for example an allow-list of controlling station addresses. A connection for which f returns false is closed before any protocol exchange.

#### func WithCommonAddrs

```go
func WithCommonAddrs(addrs ...asdu.CommonAddr) Option
```

WithCommonAddrs declares the common addresses this station answers to. An ASDU for any other address, except the broadcast address, is rejected with cause "unknown common address" before it reaches the [Handler](#type-handler). Without this option every common address is passed to the handler.

#### func WithEventQueue

```go
func WithEventQueue(size int) Option
```

WithEventQueue sets how many events each redundancy group buffers for [Server.Enqueue](#func-server-enqueue). When the queue is full the oldest event is dropped. Default DefaultEventQueue.

#### func WithLogger

```go
func WithLogger(l iec104.Logger) Option
```

WithLogger sets the logger. Nil, the default, disables logging.

#### func WithMaxSessions

```go
func WithMaxSessions(n int) Option
```

WithMaxSessions limits the number of simultaneous connections. Further connections are closed immediately after accept. Zero, the default, means no limit.

#### func WithMetrics

```go
func WithMetrics(m iec104.Metrics) Option
```

WithMetrics sets the metrics callbacks. Nil, the default, disables them.

#### func WithParams

```go
func WithParams(p apci.Params) Option
```

WithParams sets the protocol parameters k, w and t1..t3; t0 bounds the TLS handshake of an accepted connection. Zero K, W, T1 and T2 take their defaults; a zero T3 disables the idle test. The values must match the configuration of the controlling stations.

#### func WithRedundancyGroups

```go
func WithRedundancyGroups(groups ...RedundancyGroup) Option
```

WithRedundancyGroups declares the redundancy groups of the station. A connection belongs to the first group that allows its address; one that no group allows is closed before any protocol exchange.

Without this option there is one group, "default", for every client. It is only a queue: its connections are independent sessions, each with its own STARTDT and STOPDT, and none is closed because another one started.

#### func WithSecurity

```go
func WithSecurity(newEndpoint func(group string, aim uint16) (*sec.Endpoint, error)) Option
```

WithSecurity applies the application-layer security of IEC 62351-5 (IEC TS 60870-5-7) to every connection.

The station keeps one association per controlling station, which names itself by the AIM in every security message. newEndpoint makes the association when a controlling station is first heard in a redundancy group ("default" without [WithRedundancyGroups](#func-withredundancygroups)); it must return an endpoint with the role sec.Controlled, or an error to refuse that AIM. Give each AIM a sec.Trust that accepts only that station's certificate (sec.Trust.Subjects or a pinned certificate), and the sec.Config.Roles it may exercise. The connections of one controlling station in a group (a client redundancy group) share its association, carried by the one with data transfer started; other controlling stations have their own. A connection is bound to an association by the first security message it carries; until then the station sends nothing on it.

With security, an ASDU that is not protected is discarded, the [Handler](#type-handler) sees only the verified application data, and what the station sends waits until the controlling station has established a session. A request that the roles of the association do not permit is answered with a negative confirmation with cause [asdu.CauseNotAuthorized](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/otfabric/go-iec104/asdu#CauseNotAuthorized) before it reaches the Handler. Security can be combined with [WithTLS](#func-withtls).

#### func WithStateHandler

```go
func WithStateHandler(f func(s *Session, state iec104.State, err error)) Option
```

WithStateHandler registers a callback for session state changes: [iec104.StateStopped](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/otfabric/go-iec104#StateStopped) when a connection is accepted and after STOPDT, [iec104.StateStarted](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/otfabric/go-iec104#StateStarted) after STARTDT and [iec104.StateDisconnected](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/otfabric/go-iec104#StateDisconnected) when the session ends, with err holding the reason (nil when the server closed it).

For one session the callback and the [Handler](#type-handler) run on the same goroutine, in protocol order.

#### func WithTLS

```go
func WithTLS(cfg *tls.Config) Option
```

WithTLS makes [Server.ListenAndServe](#func-server-listenandserve) accept TLS connections, as profiled by IEC 62351-3. Set cfg.ClientAuth to tls.RequireAndVerifyClientCert to authenticate controlling stations. It has no effect on [Server.Serve](#func-server-serve), which uses the listener it is given.

### type RedundancyGroup

```go
type RedundancyGroup struct {
	// Name identifies the group in [Session.Group], logs and
	// [Server.Pending].
	Name string

	// Allow lists the clients that belong to the group, as IP addresses
	// ("10.0.0.5") or prefixes ("10.0.0.0/24"). An empty list accepts any
	// client that no earlier group claimed, so a catch-all group goes last.
	Allow []string
}
```

RedundancyGroup declares a redundancy group of a controlled station: the connections of one controlling station (or of several that back each other up), of which one has data transfer started at a time (IEC 60870-5-104 edition 2, clause 10, "Redundant connections"). A STARTDT on another connection takes over: the connection that was started is closed, so that nothing more is sent on it. Closing it is how this package keeps one connection started, not a requirement taken from clause 10. One in STOPDT stays up, as a standby.

A client that is taken over and reconnects with STARTDT takes over in turn. The standbys of a group reconnect without it, as [github.com/otfabric/go-iec104/client.Group](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/otfabric/go-iec104/client#Group) does, or a client with WithAutoStart(false).

Each group has its own event queue, see [Server.Enqueue](#func-server-enqueue).

#### func (Server) Addr

```go
func (s *Server) Addr() net.Addr
```

Addr returns the address of a listener the server is serving on, or nil when there is none. It is mainly useful after listening on port 0.

#### func (Server) Broadcast

```go
func (s *Server) Broadcast(ctx context.Context, a *asdu.ASDU) (int, error)
```

Broadcast sends a to every session whose data transfer is started and returns how many sessions it was sent to. Sessions in STOPDT are skipped: buffering events for them is the application's decision.

The sessions are served one after the other. A session whose send window is full blocks until its controlling station acknowledges, ctx ends or the session times out (t1). Errors of individual sessions are joined.

#### func (Server) Close

```go
func (s *Server) Close() error
```

Close stops listening and closes every session, as [Session.Close](#func-session-close) does: when it returns no handler is running or will run. Serve returns ErrServerClosed. Close is idempotent.

#### func (Server) Dropped

```go
func (s *Server) Dropped(group string) uint64
```

Dropped returns how many events a redundancy group has dropped because its queue was full.

#### func (Server) Enqueue

```go
func (s *Server) Enqueue(a *asdu.ASDU) error
```

Enqueue queues an event (spontaneous or periodic data) for every redundancy group. Each group delivers its queue, in order, to the one connection that has data transfer started, and keeps an event until the controlling station has acknowledged it:

  - while no connection of a group is started, events wait in the queue;
  - when the active connection is lost or stopped before it acknowledged an event, the event is sent again on the next active connection, so a controlling station may see an event twice across a switchover but does not miss one;
  - when the queue is full ([WithEventQueue](#func-witheventqueue)) the oldest event is dropped.

Enqueue never blocks. Compare [Server.Broadcast](#func-server-broadcast), which sends immediately to every started session and buffers nothing.

#### func (Server) ListenAndServe

```go
func (s *Server) ListenAndServe(addr string) error
```

ListenAndServe listens on the TCP address addr and serves connections until the server is closed. An empty addr means ":2404", or ":19998" with [WithTLS](#func-withtls). It always returns a non-nil error: ErrServerClosed after [Server.Close](#func-server-close).

#### func (Server) Pending

```go
func (s *Server) Pending(group string) int
```

Pending returns the number of events a redundancy group holds: queued, or sent and not yet acknowledged. An unknown name returns 0.

Serve accepts connections on ln and serves them until the server is closed. It takes ownership of ln and always returns a non-nil error: ErrServerClosed after [Server.Close](#func-server-close). Serve may be called on several listeners.

Session is one connection from a controlling station. It is safe for concurrent use.

#### func (Session) Close

```go
func (s *Session) Close() error
```

Close closes the connection. When it returns the [Handler](#type-handler) and the state handler have been called for this session for the last time: a call in progress has returned and none follows. It may be called from a handler, which it then cannot wait for; a handler must not close another session whose handler closes this one. Close is idempotent.

#### func (Session) Security

```go
func (s *Session) Security() *sec.Endpoint
```

Security returns the association of the controlling station on this session: nil without [WithSecurity](#func-withsecurity), and until the station's first security message has bound the session to its association. Every ASDU a Handler sees has been verified by it.

#### func (Session) Send

```go
func (s *Session) Send(ctx context.Context, a *asdu.ASDU) error
```

Send transmits one ASDU to the controlling station. It fails with [iec104.ErrNotStarted](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/otfabric/go-iec104#ErrNotStarted) while data transfer is stopped, and blocks while the send window is full (k unacknowledged I frames) until the peer acknowledges, ctx ends or the session ends.

#### func (Session) Started

```go
func (s *Session) Started() bool
```

Started reports whether the controlling station has started data transfer on this session.

#### func (Session) Terminate

```go
func (s *Session) Terminate(req *asdu.ASDU) error
```

Terminate sends the "activation termination" of req, which concludes an interrogation or a command execution.
